reader_notes: Short single-question unit; the mechanism (crack tears capsule, slurry seeps out, reacts with moisture, hardens into calcite) is described in one clean causal chain with no contradictions.

The passage pre-empts two distractors explicitly ('not a rise in temperature, and not any chemical brushed on afterward'), which makes A and C a little easy to eliminate; the only real competition is D, since moisture genuinely is part of the reaction but is not the trigger. That trigger-vs-participant distinction is what the item actually tests, and the text states it clearly.
Spelling is consistently American within the unit ('millimeter'), which differs from the British variety used in elf-b2-002; not an in-unit problem but worth a batch-level glance.

Named institute (Halvorsen Institute for Applied Materials) is close in shape to the 'Halvard Institute' in elf-b2-001; harmless, but the two invented institutes are easy to confuse if the units are ever seen together.
